recentItems.title: Rising sea levels projected to cost $29b each year
recentItems.description:
Rising sea levels could cost Australia more than $850 billion this century, with Queensland flagged as having the greatest number of properties at risk. 

It's an issue impacting coastal communities across the globe, with questions looming over climate change adaptation. 

With a culture of beach-side living, experts are calling for greater investment in protecting those on the coast.

recentItems.title: Lambie blasts Hanson over Hastie ‘traitor’ cartoon
recentItems.description:

Opposition leader Angus Taylor has called for the social media video to be taken down. 

It comes as the Coalition says they will oppose the government's world-first digital duty of care laws in their current form on the grounds of free speech.

recentItems.title: Lambie calls Hanson a 'coward' amid growing storm over political cartoon
recentItems.description:
Independent senator Jacqui Lambie has branded Pauline Hanson a "coward" over a One Nation cartoon labelling Liberal MP Andrew Hastie a "traitor" for giving evidence against former SAS soldier Ben Roberts-Smith.

Hanson's cartoon has drawn condemnation from across the political spectrum, with even fellow One Nation senator Barnaby Joyce saying he did not consider defence veteran Hastie a traitor.

Lambie, herself a veteran, said the video is an attack on all who have served.

The video is part of a political cartoon series created by One Nation titled Please Explain, which periodically targets politicians from various parties while promoting One Nation.

"She should remove that one of Hastie down right now today," Lambie told ABC Radio National on Thursday morning.

recentItems.title: Trump vows to give US$5,000 to US citizens if Republicans win the midterms
recentItems.description:
United States President Donald Trump has promised to give every adult US citizen US$5,000 if the Republican Party wins the upcoming midterm election in an extraordinary attempt to persuade voters to back his party. ‘

He did not say where the money would come from — with the theoretical bill likely topping US$1.35 trillion (AU$1.85 trillion) — citing only that "our country is making so much money". 

Speaking to the Republican midterm convention audience in Dallas, he likened the payments to a corporation's distributions to shareholders, citing "our tremendous strength and success economically". 

It remains unclear how the payments would work or whether they would even be legal, as the US Congress would need to approve them or otherwise acquiesce. 

The sum would far exceed US tariff revenues even before the Supreme Court tossed much of the president’s tariff program last year. 

Read more: https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/donald-trumps-only-condition-for-5000-payments-to-every-american/d6s75zh5b

recentItems.title: ‘The adventure of a lifetime’: Winner of Alone Australia S4 reflects on their journey
recentItems.description:
The winner of season four of Alone Australia has shared how a change in perspective helped them get through weeks in the Finnish wilderness.

Trent Fenton outlasted nine other contestants in the Arctic Circle to take home the title.

Fenton said seeing news reports about what was occurring in Gaza in the days leading up to his departure for the program helped put what he was experiencing into perspective.

“Think about the people like that in the real world that are doing it tough and aren’t living out the adventure of a lifetime,” Fenton said.

recentItems.title: Australian students’ record worst-ever maths and reading PISA results
recentItems.description:
Australian high school students have recorded their worst maths and reading results in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) exams.

Australian 15-year-olds have sat for the international standardized exams every three years since 2000.

While the most recent results show that Australian students are performing above their peers in many developed economies, global scores are at their lowest since testing began.

SBS World News Reporter Abbie O'Brien explains.
